other_conditions: Victim or claimant must report the crime to the officer‑in‑charge of the local police station or to the Magistrate before making a claim
Victim or claimant must fully cooperate with police and prosecution throughout the investigation and trial; turning hostile or refusing to appear is considered non‑cooperation
The crime must involve mental or bodily injury or death of the victim
Death or permanent incapacitation must not be a result of suicide, self‑infliction, or the victim’s own wrongdoing
Victim must not have received compensation for the loss or injury under any other Central or State government scheme, insurance company, or other institution
Perpetrators of the crime or their dependents are not eligible for compensation
If the offender is not traced or identified, the victim may apply for compensation under sub‑section (4) of section 357‑A of the Act
benefits_summary: Provides financial compensation (₹50,000 – ₹10,00,000) based on the type of injury, degree of disability and age of the victim, along with shelter, counseling, medical, legal, education and vocational support services.
documents_required: Copy of Final Form of investigation
